_README: SAS Core Curriculum, catalog year 2026-2027.
TWO AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, each for a different fact:
1. GOAL DEFINITIONS + REQUIREMENT STRUCTURE (this file, curated):
sasoue.rutgers.edu/core/core-learning-goals - the SAS Office of
Undergraduate Education publishes the goals, their official codes,
their wording, the area groupings, and the credit/course counts.
Published as prose, so this structure is a HUMAN DERIVATION and every
node carries the sentence it came from.
2. COURSE -> GOAL ELIGIBILITY (NOT in this file):
Rutgers SOC `coreCodes`, which publishes certification as structured
data. Eligibility is ingested from the SOC archive, never curated by
hand - a hand-maintained course list would be stale within a term.
CODES NOT INCLUDED, and why:
SOEHS  School of Engineering humanities/social science - not SAS Core
GVT    'SEBS Core: Government/Regulatory Analysis' - SEBS, not SAS
ECN    'SEBS Core: Economic Analysis' - SEBS, not SAS
CE     description literally reads 'Non-Core: Community Engagement'
ITR    'Information Technology and Research' - certified on 34 courses in
SOC but NOT listed as a current goal by either official SAS page.
Recorded as a SOURCE CONFLICT rather than guessed at.
WC     'Writing and Communication 01:355:101' - 3 courses in SOC, not
listed as a current goal. Also a source conflict.
CASE NOTE: the official page writes WCR/WCD; SOC writes WCr/WCd. Same
goals. Matching is case-insensitive on the code - see the normalizer.

program_version._why: Applied to the TARGET version. Core is the reason it must share.
program_version.source_prose: A course used to meet core goals may also be used to fulfill a major or minor requirement.

goals.name: Diversities and Social Inequalities
goals.description: Analyze the degree to which forms of human differences and stratifications among social groups shape individual and group experiences of, and perspectives on, contemporary issues.

goals.name: Our Common Future
goals.description: Analyze a contemporary global issue from a multidisciplinary perspective.

goals.name: Natural Sciences
goals.description: Understand and apply basic principles and concepts in the physical or biological sciences.

goals.name: Historical Analysis
goals.description: Explain the development of some aspect of a society or culture over time.

goals.name: Social Analysis
goals.description: Understand different theories about human culture, social identity, economic entities, political systems, and other forms of social organization.

goals.name: Philosophical and Theoretical Issues
goals.description: Examine critically philosophical and other theoretical issues concerning the nature of reality, human experience, knowledge, value, and/or cultural production.

goals.name: Arts and Literatures
goals.description: Analyze arts and/or literatures in themselves and in relation to specific histories, values, languages, cultures, and technologies.

goals.name: Nature of Languages
goals.description: Understand the nature of human languages and their speakers.

goals.name: Critical Creative Expression
goals.description: Engage critically in the process of creative expression.

goals.name: Writing and Communication, Revision
goals.description: Communicate complex ideas effectively, in standard written English, to a general audience, and respond effectively to editorial feedback from peers, instructors, &/or supervisors through successive drafts & revision.

goals.name: Writing and Communication in a Discipline
goals.description: Communicate effectively in modes appropriate to a discipline or area of inquiry; evaluate and critically assess sources and use the conventions of attribution and citation correctly; and analyze and synthesize information and ideas from multiple sources to generate new insights.

goals.name: Quantitative Information
goals.description: Formulate, evaluate, and communicate conclusions and inferences from quantitative information.

goals.name: Mathematical or Formal Reasoning
goals.description: Apply effective and efficient mathematical or other formal processes to reason and to solve problems.

requirements.name: SAS Core Curriculum
requirements.source_prose: Students generally will complete the core in 10 to 14 courses of 3 or 4 credits each.

requirements.name: Contemporary Challenges
requirements.source_prose: Contemporary Challenges (2 courses required; 1 from each category)

requirements.name: Natural Sciences
requirements.notes: The source states credits (6) but no course count for NS, so this is modeled as a credit requirement rather than inventing a number of courses.

requirements.name: Historical and Social Analysis
requirements.source_prose: Historical and Social Analysis (6 credits; 2 courses required)

requirements.name: Arts and the Humanities
requirements.notes: Two INDEPENDENT conditions: min_count=2 courses AND min_distinct_categories=2 goals. A single course certified for two AH goals therefore cannot satisfy the area on its own - it is one course.
requirements.source_prose: Arts and the Humanities [AH] (6 credits) Students must take two degree credit-bearing courses and meet at least two of these goals.

requirements.name: Writing and Communication
requirements.source_prose: Writing and Communication (9 credits; 3 courses required)

requirements.name: Quantitative and Formal Reasoning
requirements.source_prose: Quantitative and Formal Reasoning (6 credits; 2 courses required)

target_program._why: Core requirements are attached to the STUDENT'S program version, tagged requirement_system='core'. They are not a separate program: the audit engine evaluates one ProgramVersion, and sharing only works when major and core requirements live in the same tree.
